fields.note: 30-day visa-free. Max 90 days in any 180-day period. From 1 November, if you travel without a visa you should apply for an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) through the QazETA portal. Until 30 June, if you arrive without one you will not be refused entry but will be told of the requirement; from 1 July 2027 the ETA is mandatory for all visa-free nationals and you will be refused entry without one. The ETA is free, valid for 180 days from issue, and does not extend your visa-free stay. Not needed if you are under 16 or over 65, staying in the airport transit area without crossing the border, travelling on a diplomatic or service passport, or holding a valid Kazakh visa or residence permit.

fields.note: An International Visitor Permit is issued free on arrival to everyone except New Zealand and Australian passport holders — less than 31 days, not the less than 3 months that New Zealanders and Australians get, so don't read across from a New Zealand source. You need proof of onward travel, sufficient funds, accommodation details and a passport valid 6 months. The total stay is capped at 2 months without a continuous departure of more than six months.

No visa before travel — a New Zealand Visitor Permit is issued free at the border on the arrival card. The 3-month entitlement is tied specifically to New Zealand or Australian citizenship; other nationalities get less than 31 days. You need proof of onward travel and sufficient funds, and must be a genuine visitor not intending to work or study.

Kazakhstan has run a pilot of its Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA), QazETA, since January 2026 for visa-exempt visitors including Koreans; once the ETA is mandatory, visitors without approval are refused entry. It is not needed if you get a visa from the Kazakh embassy or consulate in Korea. Korean citizens may enter without a visa for up to 30 days after crossing the border, for a total of 60 days in each period of 180 days.
fields.apply: Apply for a QazETA ETA through its mobile app 72 hours before entry (pilot since January 2026; valid for up to 180 days). Longer stays: Not verified

fields.stay: 90 days (shared with El Salvador, Guatemala and Nicaragua)

fields.note: Visa-free for up to 90 days: the exemption for British citizens took effect on 31 October 2026 (a visa was required before that). The 90 days is shared with El Salvador, Guatemala and Nicaragua and does not restart when you cross borders. Passport must be valid 6 months after you arrive, with at least 2 blank pages. You get a 30-day entry stamp on arrival. Make sure the border officer stamps your passport, and apply at an immigration office if you need to extend. Overstaying can mean a fine before you leave.

Visa-free 90 days. Passport must have 3 blank pages and 6 months validity. ⚠️ Child travel rules — carry the original or a certified copy of the full birth certificate for any child aged 17 or under. If a child travels with only one parent, a guardian or another adult, or alone, carry parental consent or documents showing authority to travel, plus a certified copy of the consenting parent's passport or identity document.

Visa-free, but one thing catches people out: the free Digital Immigration Card is MANDATORY — complete it within the 7 days before departure; it is checked at airline check-in and again on arrival. Canadians can stay 90 days in any 180; to stay longer you must apply to Curaçao's Immigration Service for a short-stay residence permit, not a tourist extension. Proof of funds of about USD 1,000 per week may be requested. Your passport must be valid for the duration of your stay in Curaçao.

fields.apply: Not required · an Electronic Travel Authorization (QazETA) is recommended: apply no later than 72 hours before the planned travel date
fields.note: Canada is named in Kazakhstan's visa-regime table as visa-free up to 30 days for ordinary passports. Watch the cumulative caps — the 30 days is per entry, but total stay must not exceed 90 days in any 180-day period. On registration: an arrival notification is required within 3 working days, but it is the duty of the RECEIVING PARTY — your hotel or host — not you, and Kazakhstan states a foreign citizen does not need to apply to the migration service personally. Kazakhstan is piloting an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA), QazETA; Canada's advice recommends getting one before you travel. It is currently voluntary and free of charge, but may become mandatory and could carry fees. An ETA does not guarantee entry.

fields.apply: Up to 30 days: no visa needed. Apply for an ETA through the QazETA app before you travel. It is being phased in by border crossing: since 1 November 2026 at Aktau airport and the land crossings Urljutobe, Auhatty, Atameken and Nurly Zhol; from 1 January 2027 at Astana and Almaty airports; from 1 March 2027 at all other crossings; mandatory from 1 July 2027. Longer than 30 days: visa applied for in advance at a Kazakh embassy or consulate
fields.note: No visa is needed for stays up to 30 days. An ETA via the QazETA app is being phased in by border crossing and becomes mandatory on 1 July 2027; until then travellers without one may be told they need it but, according to the Kazakh authorities, are not refused entry. A stay beyond 30 days needs a visa applied for in advance at a Kazakh embassy or consulate.

fields.note: No visa is needed for stays up to 30 days on a Dutch passport. You may need an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA); the Dutch advice points to the QazETA website. Longer stays need a visa from the Kazakh Embassy in The Hague. Passport must be valid at least 6 months from departure.

fields.blurb: A new decree, Disposición No. 002-2026, took effect on 16 February 2026 and reshuffled which nationalities need a visa, so treat older answers as unreliable. Nicaragua is also in the CA-4 zone: the 90-day allowance is shared with Guatemala, Honduras and El Salvador and does not reset at those borders.

Passports need three blank pages and six months' validity. Child travel rules are unusually strict: carry the original or a certified copy of the full birth certificate for any child aged 17 or under, plus parental consent or documents showing authority to travel when a child travels with one parent, a guardian, another adult or alone.

A free visitor permit is issued at the border: less than 31 days for most nationalities, three months for New Zealand and Australian citizens, so New Zealand sources do not read across. You need proof of onward travel and sufficient funds, and work or study is not allowed. Extensions are applied for locally and carry a fee.
